assertions.description:
Checks that during the load phase (load_en=1 for 144 consecutive cycles),
done remains 0 throughout the load phase and only rises after the load
completes and encryption finishes. This is the observable consequence of
the serial shift: the module must accept exactly 144 bits before proceeding.
assertions.name: load_phase_serial_shift

assertions.description:
Checks that done is never asserted before at least 144+32=176 cycles have
elapsed from the start of a load sequence, confirming that encryption starts
automatically after the 144th load bit and takes exactly 32 cycles.
assertions.name: encrypt_auto_start

assertions.description:
Checks that done is asserted exactly 32 cycles after the 144th load bit,
which is the observable consequence of executing exactly 32 encryption
cycles (31 full rounds + 1 final addRoundKey). Also verifies done stays
low during the 32 encryption cycles.
assertions.name: encrypt_round_sequence

assertions.description:
Checks that done is asserted exactly on the 32nd encryption cycle after
the load phase completes, confirming the final addRoundKey step occurs
and produces the ciphertext. This is verified by checking done timing
relative to the end of the 144-cycle load phase.
assertions.name: final_add_round_key

assertions.description:
Checks that done is asserted after the 32nd encryption cycle and held
high until rst_n is deasserted or load_en begins a new load. Verifies
done persistence and correct clearing conditions.
assertions.name: done_assertion

assertions.description:
Checks that when done=1 and shift_out_en=1, dout presents valid ciphertext
bits MSB-first. Collects all dout bits during the unload phase and verifies
they form a consistent 64-bit sequence. Also cross-checks against PRESENT-80
test vectors when the input pattern matches a known test vector.
assertions.name: unload_serial_shift

assertions.description:
Checks that whenever rst_n transitions to 0, done is cleared in the
immediately following observed output (asynchronous clear). Also checks
that done does not appear while rst_n is held low.
assertions.name: async_reset_behavior

assertions.description:
Checks that when load_en is asserted while done=1, done is cleared on
the next rising clock edge and the module begins a fresh load sequence.
assertions.name: load_en_restarts_operation

assertions.description:
Checks that dout is only architecturally meaningful when both done=1 and
shift_out_en=1. When done=0 or shift_out_en=0, dout should be 0 or hold
its last driven value (we check it is not toggling unexpectedly when
shift_out_en=0 and done=0, i.e., it should be stable at 0 outside unload).
assertions.name: dout_valid_only_during_unload

rationale_notes: The assertions here operate on the observable port signals only (clk, rst_n, load_en, din, shift_out_en, dout, done).
Internal signals (key_reg, state, FSM state, counters) are not directly observable, so we infer behaviour from the port-level stimulus/response trace.
For test_vector_correctness we implement the full PRESENT-80 algorithm in pure Python and compare against the collected dout bits.
load_phase_serial_shift and encrypt_round_sequence cannot be fully verified from ports alone; we check what is observable (timing, done assertion, dout correctness).
Cycle indexing: stim[i] holds the input values presented at cycle i; observed[i] holds the output values sampled at cycle i (after the rising edge).
We treat each list entry as one clock cycle. rst_n=0 in stim means reset is asserted during that cycle.
